items.problem: The skill's 'Defensive UI for device-dependent features' rule instructs agents to 'swap the page's main content for the fallback' when a device is absent. The migration agent followed it verbatim (FallbackText matches the skill's example sentence), collapsing all scenario controls (Enable/Disable/Get Data + altitude output) when GetDefault() returns null. Both scenarios scored fail; every interactive control is missing from the WinUI UIA tree.
items.evidence: migration-score.json (features_fail:2, both 'fail', winui_responded:false); discrepancies.json id=global-fallback-overrides-scenarios; migrated Scenario1_DataEvents.xaml.cs ShowFallback() collapses MainContent; original UWP Scenario1_DataEvents.xaml.cs keeps controls and calls NotifyUser('No altimeter found').
items.root_cause: The rule prescribes REPLACING the page's main content (contradicting the Fidelity rule) and is applied to the normal null-GetDefault() no-device path that UWP samples handle without hiding controls.
items.change: Rewrote SKILL.md 'Defensive UI for device-dependent features' into two rules: (1) preserve the original's device-absent behaviour — a null GetDefault() is normal, report via the existing status/NotifyUser mechanism and NEVER hide/collapse/replace controls the original renders unconditionally; (2) add an ADDITIVE fallback only when init can throw or the page would otherwise be blank, surfaced via the status region or a TextBlock alongside the controls — never Visibility.Collapsed on main content. Added a falsifiable check requiring the same named controls in the WinUI UIA tree even with no device.
items.expected_effect: Migration agents reproduce the original's device-absent handling, leaving all scenario controls present and interactive on a device-less validation box across the whole sensor/hardware sample family.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run, the WinUI UIA tree for each scenario contains the same named controls as the source (e.g. ScenarioEnableButton, ScenarioDisableButton, 'Get Data') even with no altimeter; requirements 1-4 go fail->pass and no global 'requires a ... device' message replaces the controls. Tier-3 chosen because the defect is incorrect instructional prose — only correcting the prose can un-say wrong guidance; no script emits this fallback, so a Tier 1/2 change cannot carry it.

deferred_to_human: Eval-skill limitation (not edited): Compare-Parity counted 'Enable'/'Disable' as covered via substring match against the 'IsEnabled' UIA property, a false positive that masked the missing buttons. This belongs to winui3-parity-check (measurement instrument) and is out of scope here.
